verdict.rationale: Slate is a terminal coding agent driven by natural-language prompts. It can reference files with @filename (random-labs-docs-10), run shell commands with ! (random-labs-docs-9), deeply research a problem in parallel (random-labs-docs-26), and manually perform integration tests (random-labs-docs-16), so debugging through conversation is plausible. However, no documentation explicitly describes a debugging or troubleshooting workflow for user code; the troubleshooting page only covers reporting bugs in Slate itself. Missing for 10: explicit docs on debugging workflows (error or stack-trace analysis, root-cause investigation, fix verification), worked debugging examples, and independent or hands-on evidence of debugging effectiveness.
